answer: Cross-epoch trajectory lock. Each identity gets an inlet: the set of counterparties it transacts with in epoch N. At epoch N+1, its vertex in the interaction graph must overlap that inlet by a fixed fraction (e.g. 60%) or the identity is flagged and its rewards withheld. A sybil cluster must therefore sustain the same dense reef of recurring counterparties across every epoch, forcing the attacker to run and pay for continuous, mutually-consistent activity among all fake identities rather than one-off registrations.
